scope: Proposed observable objectives for the existing authored bus lesson. These annotations do not change narration, visual behavior or installed practice, and are not independent scientific approval.

objectives.question: Explain why a memory request needs a rule for when its answer can be accepted.
objectives.where: Distinguish the selected address from the value stored at that location.
objectives.address: Trace address 16 to its selected row without treating selection as a change to the stored value.
objectives.waiting: Explain why a number present on the bus can still be an old answer.
objectives.early: Predict the incorrect value captured by sampling too early in the illustrative model.
objectives.ready: Identify what changes when returned data becomes valid while the address stays fixed.
objectives.timing: Relate request, validity and sampling traces using their shared time axis.
objectives.takeaway: State separate questions for where to look and when to accept the answer.
objectives.ownership-0: Locate the shared-bus topology in the original course diagram.
objectives.ownership-1: Trace the address path from the processor toward the address decoders.
objectives.ownership-2: Explain how an address selects the participating slave.
objectives.ownership-3: Distinguish physical connection from permission to drive shared wires.
objectives.ownership-4: Identify the selected slave as the returned-data driver in this read.
objectives.ownership-5: Recognize that changing from a read to a write changes transfer roles.
objectives.ownership-6: Identify the data driver and receiver for a write without assuming simultaneous transmission.
objectives.ownership-7: Identify control connections that can send and receive signals in the displayed topology.
objectives.ownership-8: Explain why the DMA interface can have different roles in different transactions.
objectives.ownership-9: State the lesson's assumption that arbitration has already selected a master.
objectives.ownership-10: Predict the address driver and returned-data driver for a memory read.
objectives.ownership-11: Explain the read-ownership answer while keeping address and value distinct.
objectives.ideal-0: Separate the original course timing figure from the accompanying logical illustration.
objectives.ideal-1: Use left-to-right time and shared vertical clock guides to compare events.
objectives.ideal-2: Identify the address and control actions at event 1 in this course example.
objectives.ideal-3: Interpret the read/write signal's high level using this diagram's convention.
objectives.ideal-4: Distinguish a valid address from valid returned data.
objectives.ideal-5: Locate the negative clock edge marked event 2.
objectives.ideal-6: Explain the slave's response while the illustrative master register retains its prior value.
objectives.ideal-7: Locate event 3 without confusing a narration transition with an additional hardware delay.
objectives.ideal-8: Identify when the master stores the returned data in this ideal sequence.
objectives.ideal-9: Explain why a timing band represents multiple wires rather than one binary trace.
objectives.ideal-10: Explain why valid data can contain both zero and one bits.
objectives.ideal-11: Predict which displayed edge completes data capture at the master.
objectives.ideal-12: Justify the storage edge and state why this course sequence is not universal.
objectives.propagation-0: Recognize why the same signal is drawn separately at its two endpoints.
objectives.propagation-1: Locate the master-side and slave-side address rows on the original figure.
objectives.propagation-2: Identify the driver's contribution to address stability at the sending master.
objectives.propagation-3: Explain why master-side stability does not establish slave-side stability.
objectives.propagation-4: Interpret transition and stable regions without inventing exact arrival times.
objectives.propagation-5: Locate the return-data path on the original page-22 figure.
objectives.propagation-6: Identify selection and access at the slave before data returns to the master.
objectives.propagation-7: Distinguish internal slave Data Valid from data stability at the receiving master.
objectives.propagation-8: Trace returned data through the slave driver and bus.
objectives.propagation-9: Compare the slave-side and master-side data-valid intervals.
objectives.propagation-10: Choose the receiving master as the endpoint for its sampling requirement.
objectives.propagation-11: Identify the separate stages that contribute to the displayed return path.
objectives.propagation-12: Point to the receiving endpoint before choosing a timing inequality.
objectives.window-0: Identify the receiving register's before-edge setup requirement.
objectives.window-1: Identify the separate after-edge hold requirement.
objectives.window-2: Separate illustrative numerical inputs from course device specifications.
objectives.window-3: Identify the illustrative sampling edge, setup time and hold time with units.
objectives.window-4: Calculate the required stable interval from the edge and its two requirements.
objectives.window-5: Identify the actual data-valid interval in the separate numerical example.
objectives.window-6: Compare required and actual validity intervals on one time scale.
objectives.window-7: Calculate setup margin from actual arrival and the setup deadline.
objectives.window-8: Calculate hold margin from actual release and the hold boundary.
objectives.window-9: Explain why containment of both required boundaries passes the interval check.
objectives.window-10: Predict how delaying only data arrival changes the setup margin.
objectives.window-11: Explain why arrival before the sampling edge can still violate setup.
objectives.window-12: Predict how early release changes hold while arrival stays fixed.
objectives.window-13: Explain a hold failure that occurs despite passing setup.
objectives.window-14: State the two independent boundary checks and the limits of the interval model.
objectives.handshake-0: Identify the two ready signals that coordinate the displayed asynchronous read.

objectives.handshake-13: Explain why asynchronous sequencing does not eliminate propagation or stable-data requirements.

objectives.async-delays-6: Explain why a ready edge does not remove waiting and storage constraints.
objectives.async-delays-7: Identify the master's acknowledgement after data capture.
objectives.async-delays-8: Explain why address and control must outlast the locally deasserted ready indication.
objectives.async-delays-9: Locate the receiving master's hold requirement in the original page-40 figure.
objectives.async-delays-10: Explain why acknowledgement-controlled release still needs sufficient data validity.
objectives.async-delays-11: Use original images and one causal path to resolve dense or unreliable extracted diagrams.
